purpose: Every surface on which OOZEMeter makes a factual, causal, comparative, directional, methodological or confidence-bearing statement. A surface listed here MUST register with the claim gate before it may publish. `gated` is the load-bearing field: it records what validates the surface TODAY, not what should.

claimTypes.MEASUREMENT: Asserts a value: a score, a rate, a count, a date. Falsifiable against a named series or artifact.
claimTypes.COMPARISON: Asserts a relation between two figures (higher/lower, N of M, ranked, versus 2008).
claimTypes.TREND: Asserts a direction or magnitude of change over time (eased, jumped, held flat, climbed N points).
claimTypes.INTERPRETATION: Assigns meaning to a figure (band names, tier labels, 'Containment Held', 'relief', 'the vibecession').
claimTypes.CAUSAL: Asserts that one thing produced another (because, drove, triggered, led to, kept the declaration off the board).
claimTypes.CROSS-CHECK: Asserts that two series agree, disagree, or are mixed.
claimTypes.INDEPENDENCE: Asserts that two figures are separate, unrelated, or share no inputs.
claimTypes.NEGATIVE: Asserts absence: does not use, carries no weight, never touches, has never been met, no fake numbers.
claimTypes.CONFIDENCE: Asserts the reliability of the pipeline itself (gate passed, feeds current, every figure traces, fails closed).
claimTypes.METHODOLOGY: Asserts how the number is built (weights, anchors, calibration, transforms, version).
claimTypes.FORECAST-FORWARD: Asserts or disclaims something about the future (leads, predicts, next month, 'we do not forecast').
claimTypes.UNCERTAINTY: Asserts the limits of a figure (provisional, experimental, proxy, may lag, reconstruction not vintage).

gateStatusValues.full: Every claim on this surface is checked by a program before publication.
gateStatusValues.partial: Some claim classes are checked; at least one named class can reach production unvalidated.
gateStatusValues.none: No program reads this surface for truth. Human review only.

findings.title: articles.js publishes two different counts for the same month, and the release gate's presence test blesses both
findings.evidence: articles.js:280 — 'at the crisis peak of June 2009, with the overall score at {{s:2009-06}}, five of six lines had crossed the emergency threshold.' articles.js:27 — 'At the GFC's worst (June 2009), six of seven lines crossed 60.' notes.html:52 — 'six of seven lines crossed 60'. research/backtest-results.json 2009-06: employment 78.2, housing 86.7, credit 89.7, auto 93.5, gas 61.8, financial 69.1 all above 60; inflation 56.4 below. Six of seven.
findings.whyItSurvived: 'five of six' was correct under methodology v2's six weighted lines. v3 added Financial Conditions. release-gate.js ALREADY BANS the phrase by name — but only in notes.html: `if(/\ball six lines\b/i.test(notes)||/five of six/i.test(notes)||!/six of seven/i.test(notes))`. For articles.js it only requires that /six of seven/i appear SOMEWHERE; it appears at line 27, so the gate is satisfied while the banned phrase sits 253 lines below in the same file.
findings.gateGap: There is no consistency check across a corpus — only presence checks within it. The correct assertion was written and pointed at one of the two files that needed it.

findings.title: archive.html publishes a score literal that is wrong by 8 points, on a surface the score-literal ban never scans
findings.evidence: archive.html:140 — 'so the jar read just 27'. data/history.json 2022-06 = 19. Highest 2022 reading = 24. The narrative gate's own CLAIM regex matches the string 'read just 27' and would fail the build; narrative-check.js:105-113 scans articles.js, auto-articles and reconstruction-reports only, and never opens archive.html.
findings.whyItSurvived: The ban was scoped to article corpora. archive.html carries its own inline EV[] array of event prose, rendered through resolveClaims into #epDesc on every event click.
findings.gateGap: The score-literal ban must run over every reader surface, not three corpora.

findings.title: index.html overwrites the gate-derived integrity placard with a hardcoded PASS on every page load
findings.evidence: index.html:239 — $('plcSealed').textContent='Integrity gate: PASS · fails closed'. stamp.js:18-37 reads data/gate-status.json, refuses to stamp when status!=='pass' or the verdict month is stale, and appends '· N warnings'. All of that is discarded by the client.
findings.whyItSurvived: stamp.js's fix was applied to the static markup. The runtime assignment was left in place, so the two disagree and the runtime wins.
findings.gateGap: No test asserts that a CONFIDENCE string on a reader surface derives from an artifact rather than a literal.
findings.liveFalsehood: Not today (the gate passes), but the claim is unconditional and would be false the moment it mattered — plus it silently suppresses the warnings disclosure.

findings.title: Every NEGATIVE and INDEPENDENCE claim on the site is enforced by a code comment or a string, never by a program
findings.evidence: At least 14 distinct published sentences of the form 'does not use / carries no score weight / never touches / has never been met / the only input in common'. The pair-legality rule that D1 violated is stated in a comment at scripts/story.js:118-123: 'Every pair added here must be verified absent from scripts/collect.js first.' That verification is a human instruction. scripts/lib/dependency-graph.js can decide it in one call and nothing in the publish pipeline calls it.
findings.gateGap: The graph exists, passes 11 tests, and is wired into zero gates. It is a test, not a gate.

findings.title: Claim scanning covers 3 of ~50 narrative surfaces
findings.evidence: narrative-check.js scans articles.js, data/auto-articles.js, data/reconstruction-reports.js for claims, plus feed.xml and index.html for token leaks. Unscanned: notes.html, what-is-ooze.html, about.html, policies.html, market.html, archive.html, states.html, personal.html, terms.html, privacy.html, specimen-progress.html, oozeonomics.html, 404.html, data/editorial.json prose, editorial.newsletter, editorial.social, scripts/lib/market-gauge-content.js, all 6 market/<gauge>/ pages, all 6 lesson pages, all 9 /<slug>/ static pages, all 44 /files/ pages, the weekly email and Discord bodies, og-cards, and every aria-label and sr-only string on the site.
findings.gateGap: Surface coverage is opt-in and undocumented. data/claim-surfaces.json is the registry that makes it opt-out.

findings.title: editorial.json is exempt from the token scan, is a public artifact, and carries two fields that no resolver anywhere will ever read
findings.evidence: narrative-check.js:209 skips data/editorial.json in the reader-surface token scan, correctly, because it is a token CARRIER. But editorial.newsletter contains BOTH the baked literal 'OOZE LEVEL: 26/100' AND the unresolved token '{{s:2026-07}}' in the same string; release-gate.js:62 REQUIRES the baked literal; and grep across the repo finds no consumer of editorial.newsletter or editorial.social at all. The Buttondown wiring is an open task (flowmap.html:1119).
findings.gateGap: Three individually correct rules jointly guarantee that whoever wires the email path ships a stale literal or a raw token — the exact failure that reached RSS subscribers on 2026-08-14.

findings.title: The daily workflow stamps market.html and then throws the stamp away
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/collect.yml:53 — `git add data/market-history.json data/market-history.js data/ index.html feed.xml lab.js`. market.html is not in the list. scripts/stamp.js:123 writes it every run and counts its markers into `missing`, which exits 1.
findings.gateGap: Nothing asserts that every file a publish script writes is a file the publish workflow commits.
findings.liveFalsehood: The pre-JS market score served to crawlers and link previews is whatever was last hand-committed.

findings.title: A screen-reader label contradicts the sighted copy on the same chart, and the test suite enforces only the sighted one
findings.evidence: lab.js:340 aria-label='20-year stress history chart'. archive.html:31 and tests/public-labels.test.js:32 both assert '23 years of measured U.S. economic stress'.
findings.gateGap: No gate reads accessibility strings. D2's most durable half lived in exactly this class.

findings.title: A simulated array reaches a personal reading with no label on the output
findings.evidence: personal.html:105 stateStress = stateScore/100*20 where stateScore comes from lab.js STATES ('demo state stress scores'). The result renders on the same jar component as the national score, is compared to it in the verdict line, and is copied to the clipboard as 'MY PERSONAL OOZE: X/100' with no marker. about.html publishes 'No fake numbers, ever.'
findings.gateGap: public-labels.test.js checks that states.html carries the SIMULATED label. Nothing checks the surfaces that CONSUME the simulated array.
findings.scopeNote: OUT OF SCOPE for repair. Inventoried.

findings.title: Hand-typed historical measurements sit one array away from the pattern that would validate them
findings.evidence: lab.js EVENTS[] publishes 10.0% unemployment, 14.8%, 22M jobs, 6.1M weekly claims, 9.1% CPI — all checkable against series the collector already downloads, none checked. lab.js INCIDENTS[] on the next line has its `peak` recomputed from history by release-gate.js:132-141 and fails the build on drift. notes.html:52 publishes seven per-line June 2009 stress figures with the same exposure.
findings.gateGap: The recompute-and-fail pattern exists in the repo and was applied to one array.

findings.title: The site's foundational causal model is asserted, unfalsifiable by its own instrument, and ungated
findings.evidence: 'Ooze is economic stress moving through a household's defenses — in a fixed order. Every budget fails the same way, one line at a time.' Six ordered steps, each named as the cause of the next. The Ooze Score is a weighted blend of contemporaneous levels; it does not measure sequence and cannot falsify the claim.
findings.gateGap: There is no gate class for CAUSAL claims at all. 34 causal constructions in the article corpus alone.

findings.title: Two ranking algorithms for the same list on the same page
findings.evidence: index.html:260 byContribution sorts with weight and slug tiebreaks and is documented as reproducible. index.html:453 sorts the share card's top3 by bare contrib across all nine INDICATORS including zero-weight auxiliaries.
findings.gateGap: Nothing asserts that two surfaces describing the same ordering use the same comparator.

counts.note: Two surfaces of sixty-two are fully validated: data/reconstruction-reports.js (every printed reading reconciled against published history) and data/gate-status.json (a recorded verdict rather than an asserted one). Thirty have no program reading them for truth at all.

registrationRule: A surface may publish only if it appears in `surfaces[]` with a non-empty `validation[]` covering every entry in its `claimTypes[]`. Adding prose to an unregistered surface, or adding a claimType to a registered surface without a matching validation rule, must fail the build. `gated: "none"` is the current state of 30 of the 62 registered surfaces and is the backlog this registry exists to burn down.
priorityOrder: CI-1 and CI-2 are live falsehoods on public pages today and are fixable by widening the existing narrative-check corpus set to every reader surface.
CI-3 is a one-line deletion in index.html plus a test asserting the placard derives from data/gate-status.json.
CI-4 is the D1 class and needs the dependency graph wired into scripts/story.js as a hard precondition on CC_PAIRS, not a comment.
CI-6 and CI-7 are pre-staged failures: neither has fired yet, both will fire the moment someone completes an already-planned task.
